profile.reading: This is Roma Capitales own municipal data center, operated by the citys Dipartimento Trasformazione Digitale, or Department of Digital Transformation, which runs a dedicated Data Center Operations, Cloud Services, and Digital Signatures office to manage it. An IBM case study published in May 2024 describes the environments scale as roughly 800 virtual machines and 150 physical machines, running a mixed bare metal, container, and Hyper-V infrastructure, managed by a five person team under a Head of Data Center, with IBM Turbonomic software deployed for hybrid cloud optimization that the city credits with cutting on premises RAM and CPU usage by about 15 percent and hardware costs by about 10 percent. No public source discloses this facilitys power capacity in megawatts, technical floor space, or a specific build or opening year, an honest gap this registry records rather than estimates. The facility underpins Romes broader digital administration strategy, run through the citys Agenda Digitale and the Roma Data Platform, an open source data platform integrating internet of things sensors, artificial intelligence, and cloud services across mobility, tourism, and governance functions alongside a unified citizen portal and customer relationship management system, forming what the city describes as its smart city and safe city digital backbone. This municipal facility is distinct from a separate, unrelated development sometimes covered in Italian trade press describing Rome becoming a commercial data center hub, referring to private sector projects such as Digital Realtys reported 40 million euro campus in the Trigoria area, which is not part of, or operated by, Roma Capitale itself. This registrys research this session relied on public sector procurement, vendor case study, and city administration sources rather than a dedicated public facility fact sheet, consistent with the more limited public disclosure typical of internal municipal government IT infrastructure compared with commercial colocation providers.
